title: private-installer: implement `rollback` command (chart pin + snapshot restore w/ guardrails)
author: Devon Price
release_notes: Private installer: add `rollback` command with deterministic ordering, safety checks (migration + snapshot presence), and interactive/non-interactive operator UX.
body:
Summary This PR adds a first-cut rollback workflow to redwood-private-installer. The new `rollback` command re-applies the previously known-good chart versions and restores the last verified control-plane snapshot (when safe), with explicit guardrails to prevent unsafe downgrades (e.g., forward-only DB migrations). This closes the operator loop for the upgrade controller work introduced in PRs #418 (upgrade plan) and #427 (backup step).

Motivation We’ve had multiple failure modes in rehearsals/beta where an upgrade fails after some components have moved forward (gateway rollout, control plane chart change, migration job). Operators needed a deterministic and supported way to return to a known-good state without hand-editing Helm values or guessing which snapshot to restore. Support also asked for a consistent non-interactive rollback path for incidents (SUP-1842).

What’s included Command: `redwood-private rollback` with an interactive default UX and flags for automation.
- Determines rollback target: defaults to “previous known good” (PKG) recorded by the installer state store during upgrade; can be overridden via `--to-version` (bundle version) or `--to-release` (explicit chart refs).
- Validates prerequisites and refuses unsafe rollback by default: requires a verified snapshot for the target window; checks version compatibility matrix; checks migration safety (blocks if any applied migrations are marked forward-only).
- Applies rollback in deterministic order: gateway/ingress first (traffic shaping), then control plane, then runtime, then observability agents. Ordering is aligned with the upgrade framework invariants.
- Restores snapshot when required: restores control-plane DB snapshot from the backup location configured during upgrade; supports both object-store targets and on-prem/local paths. Restore is skipped if charts rollback is sufficient and the operator chooses `--no-restore`.
- Post-rollback validation: runs a smoke suite (API health endpoints + basic auth path), waits for deployments to become Ready, and prints a clear “rollback succeeded / rollback incomplete” report.
- Diagnostics: emits a rollback report artifact that can be attached to Support escalations (summary + step timings + key errors).

New CLI and flags Examples:
- Interactive rollback to previous known good: `redwood-private rollback`
- Non-interactive (for automation / runbooks): `redwood-private rollback --yes`
- Dry run / plan output: `redwood-private rollback --dry-run`
- Roll back charts only (no DB restore): `redwood-private rollback --no-restore`
- Override target version: `redwood-private rollback --to-version 2025.02.0-private.3`
- Explicitly bypass migration guardrail (requires double confirm): `redwood-private rollback --force` (prints migration warning + requires `--yes` or interactive confirmation)

Guardrails and safety model This PR is intentionally conservative:
- Migration safety: uses the control plane migration metadata (via control-plane endpoint / metadata table) to detect forward-only migrations; if detected, rollback is blocked unless `--force` is provided. Even with `--force`, DB snapshot restore will only proceed if the snapshot was taken pre-migration.
- Snapshot presence and verification: rollback refuses to restore unless the snapshot record is present AND marked verified (verification step from #427). We also verify the snapshot is readable before beginning rollback steps.
- Version skew rules: enforces that chart versions match a supported compatibility tuple (control plane/runtime/gateway/observability). If the tuple is unknown, rollback aborts with a remediation hint (“import the correct offline bundle” / “use --to-release with explicit refs”).
- Operator prompts: interactive prompt shows a step-by-step plan including what will be restored and which versions will be applied. It also prints a prominent warning when `--force` is used.

Implementation notes - Installer state store now persists: last successful upgrade boundary (PKG), chart refs, and snapshot id for the upgrade attempt. Rollback reads from this state to compute the rollback plan.
- The rollback executor reuses the upgrade step graph engine but runs in reverse order with explicit “rollback-safe boundary” checks.
- Helm: uses `helm upgrade --install` with pinned chart refs rather than `helm rollback` to avoid relying on Helm release history (some customer environments prune it). We still read release history for display purposes.
- DB restore: supports postgres restore via k8s Job (same namespace as control plane). For on-prem/local backup targets, the restore job mounts the backup PV/path.

Files / areas touched (high level) - cmd/rollback.go: new command wiring + flags + UX prompts
- internal/rollback/*: rollback planner + executor
- internal/state/store.go: persist/read PKG + snapshot metadata
- internal/backup/restore.go: restore job spec + verification
- internal/compat/matrix.go: additional helpers for rollback target validation
- internal/reporting/rollback_report.go: structured report + human summary
- docs/private/rollback.md: operator docs + examples

Illustrative snippet (planner output) Example `--dry-run` output:
Plan: rollback to previous known good
- Target bundle: 2025.02.0-private.2
- Target charts: control-plane=1.42.3 runtime=2.18.1 gateway=0.31.0 obs=0.14.2
- Snapshot: cpdb-snap-2025-02-07T03:14Z (verified)
Steps:
1) Set gateway to maintenance mode + drain connections (timeout 120s)
2) Apply control-plane chart 1.42.3
3) Restore cpdb snapshot cpdb-snap-... (k8s Job redwood-cpdb-restore)
4) Apply runtime chart 2.18.1
5) Apply observability chart 0.14.2
6) Smoke tests: /healthz, /readyz, /v1/models

CI / testing - Unit tests: rollback planner (target selection, guardrails), restore job templating
- Integration: simulated mid-upgrade failure -> rollback returns service health within 15 minutes (local kind + mocked object store)
- Manual: rehearsed in staging-private-01 (see notes below)

Staging rehearsal notes - Initial attempt surfaced that our “previous known good” record wasn’t written when upgrade aborted early; fixed by writing PKG at the start of upgrade and “current attempt” separately (commit 9b1c8e7).
- Verified that rollback aborts cleanly when forward-only migration marker is present (expected), and prints exact migration ids.

Review discussion highlights - Michael Nguyen: requested stricter behavior on forward-only migrations (block by default). Implemented + added `--force` escape hatch with double confirmation.
- Kenji Nakamura: requested clearer interactive prompts and a final summary that can be copy/pasted into support tickets. Implemented: “Rollback report summary” section and consistent phrasing for errors.
- Sean Gallagher: requested non-interactive support for runbooks and CI-driven drills. Added `--yes`, `--dry-run`, and stable exit codes (0 success, 2 guardrail block, 3 partial rollback).

Checklist - [x] Linked Linear tickets
- [x] Added docs and examples
- [x] Added unit tests
- [x] Added integration test scenario (mid-upgrade failure)
- [x] Non-interactive flags and stable exit codes
- [x] Guardrails for migration + snapshot verification

Screenshots / logs Not included (CLI-only). See staging rehearsal run log attached in the internal thread referenced from ENG-2318.

How to try it Locally (dev):
1) Run an upgrade attempt that creates a snapshot: `redwood-private upgrade --to-version <X>`
2) Simulate failure mid-upgrade (or stop after control plane): `--stop-after control-plane`
3) Run `redwood-private rollback --dry-run`
4) Run `redwood-private rollback` and confirm restore

Merge notes Squash merged. Follow-up work:
- Wire rollback events into audit logging + correlation id propagation (tracked in ENG-2321 / redwood PR)
- Expand restore support for PV snapshots (on-prem environments) and add richer diagnostics bundle content (ENG-2321)
- Validate behavior with offline bundle import flow (ENG-2319)
